configuration: PHYSICS=HD; 1D CARTESIAN; 400 zones; solver hllc; LINEAR reconstruction; CHARACTERISTIC_TRACING time stepping; tstop 0.2; CFL 0.8; dbl output '90.5 -1 single_file'
variant: ic/variant/pluto.ini multiplies the [Grid] X1-grid right edge by (1 + 1e-15): 1.0 becomes 1.000000000000001, one ulp of the domain length. Every cell edge, and with it every initial value evaluated at a cell centre, moves at round-off while the physics is unchanged (the deck has no continuous initial-condition parameter to perturb), so the two runs differ by rounding only and their spread is the floor of this check.

comparison.files: grid.out (cell edges under the bound), the frame set dbl.out declares (a gate), and the final data.NNNN.dbl frame at t = tstop: every variable, staggered components included, plus its time; intermediate frames are reported, not graded, because PLUTO writes them at the first step past the dump time (Src/main.c, CheckForOutput) and two correct runs do not share that time
comparison.rule: abs(candidate - reference) <= atol + rtol * abs(reference) for every value

evidence.floor_how: nominal versus variant, sab.py task selfcheck run 20260902T065725Z (2026-09-02T06:59:14Z): largest absolute difference over every graded value 9.66e-14, largest relative difference 2.54e-08, verdict under the provisional bound: pass; measured runtime 14 s on the nominal solve with the whole suite running concurrently on 16 cores. The legacy leaf recorded two independent single-rank runs of the same binary as byte-identical.

warrant: The graded observable is the state PLUTO writes for this configuration (every variable of the final dbl frame at t = tstop, its time and the grid edges; intermediate frames must exist but are not graded, because PLUTO writes them at the first step past the dump time (Src/main.c, CheckForOutput) so their physical time depends on the step sequence), compared value by value under |candidate - reference| <= 1e-8 + 1e-8|reference|, the bound the owner approved for the merged PLUTO leaves (PR #300) and kept here as the calibration hypothesis. What the check exercises: 1D Sod problem with the HLLC solver, characteristic tracing time stepping and characteristic limiting with the MC limiter. The bound is physical because a faithful port differs from the reference only by rounding while the nearest real fault lands orders of magnitude above it: a port with a wrong contact wave speed or a primitive-variable limiter substituted for the characteristic one moves the graded state by 1e-3 to 1e-1 relative over many cells. It is achievable because the state is double precision end to end (Src/structs.h:524, the Vc array) and two legitimate runs differ only in the order of floating-point operations; the relative term sits one decade above the 1e-9 branch thresholds where a rounding difference can flip a solver decision (Src/HD/hllc.c:169, Src/MHD/hll.c:161, Src/MHD/eigenv.c:298, the small_p and small_rho floors of Src/HD/two_shock.c:29), and the absolute term is the measured floor of the components that are zero or near zero in these configurations: the calibration runs of 2026-09-02 put round-off noise on such components at 1e-11 to 4e-9 after 1e2 to 1e4 steps (a one-ulp shift of the time-step sequence times the local gradient), so 1e-8 sits a decade above that floor and five orders below any fault, while the relative term still governs every field of order unity. The measured floor of this check is the nominal-versus-variant spread recorded in evidence; where that spread exceeds the bound the policy is revised from the number, never loosened by hand.
